subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which political party formed the government in independent India continuously from 1947 to 1977 at the Centre?
options: D) The Communist Party of India
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress maintained an unbroken rule at the national level for three full decades from independence in 1947 until the March 1977 elections.

questions.question: In which state did the Praja Socialist Party (PSP) form a short-lived minority government headed by Pattom Thanu Pillai in 1954?
questions.explanation: Pattom Thanu Pillai of the PSP formed a minority ministry in Travancore-Cochin in March 1954 with external legislative support from the Congress.

questions.question: Which princely state in Gujarat witnessed a public plebiscite in February 1948 in which over 99% of voters chose to join India?
questions.explanation: Following the Nawab's departure for Pakistan, a plebiscite was conducted in Junagadh in February 1948, voting overwhelmingly in favor of accession to the Indian Union.

questions.question: The famous slogan 'Divided by boundaries, united by culture' was challenged during partition by the violent creation of which two sovereign dominions?
questions.explanation: The partition of British India into India and Pakistan on 14-15 August 1947 caused the displacement of over 8 million people and brutal communal violence.

questions.question: The First Five Year Plan covered which specific five-year operational timeframe in India?
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan was launched for the period 1951-1956, focusing on agriculture, community development, and irrigation.

questions.question: What kind of economy did India adopt during the planning era, combining features of both public ownership and private enterprise?
options: C) A Pure Soviet Command Economy
questions.explanation: India opted for a 'mixed economy' model, where the state controlled heavy and core infrastructure while the private sector operated in consumer industries and trade.

questions.question: Which international conference of 29 newly independent Asian and African states was hosted by Indonesia in April 1955?
questions.explanation: The historic Bandung Conference held in Indonesia in April 1955 laid the bedrock of Afro-Asian solidarity and the core principles of the Non-Aligned Movement.

questions.question: Which international peace agreement signed in July 1972 committed India and Pakistan to resolve all bilateral issues peacefully through bilateral negotiations?
questions.explanation: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Pakistani President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto following the Bangladesh war.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Who served as the Prime Minister of India who coined the patriotic slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' during the food crisis and the 1965 war?
questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' to boost the morale of the nation's soldiers fighting at the border and farmers producing food grains.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which Indian state witnessed the defeat of senior Congress leader K. Kamaraj in the 1967 legislative assembly elections?
questions.explanation: Congress President K. Kamaraj lost his seat in Virudhunagar in Madras State in 1967 as the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) swept to power.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In which year did the formal organizational split take place between the Syndicate-led Congress(O) and Indira Gandhi's Congress(R)?
questions.explanation: The Congress formally split in November 1969 following the bitter presidential election contest between V.V. Giri and N. Sanjiva Reddy.

questions.question: Under whose leadership was the student protest against price rise and food scarcity in Gujarat launched in January 1974?
questions.explanation: The Navnirman Movement in Gujarat began in engineering college hostels in January 1974, leading to assembly dissolution and fresh elections.

questions.question: Which Justice of the Allahabad High Court delivered the landmark verdict on 12 June 1975 invalidating Indira Gandhi's 1971 election to the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court set aside Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli for corrupt electoral practices.

questions.question: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution was passed in which year by the Shiromani Akali Dal demanding greater regional autonomy for Punjab?
questions.explanation: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution was adopted in October 1973 at Anandpur Sahib, Punjab, outlining demands for state autonomy within a federal setup.

questions.question: Under which accord signed in August 1985 did the Central Government agree to identify and deport foreigners who entered Assam after 24 March 1971?
questions.explanation: The Assam Accord was signed on 15 August 1985 between Rajiv Gandhi's government and AASU/AAGSP leaders, establishing the 1971 citizenship cut-off date.

questions.question: The Mandal Commission identified how many castes and communities across India as socially and educationally backward classes?
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission's report identified 3,743 castes and communities comprising roughly 52% of the Indian population as Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs).

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which post-communist country in the Balkans underwent violent disintegration in the 1990s, fracturing into Croatia, Bosnia, Serbia, and Slovenia?
questions.explanation: The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia collapsed in a series of brutal ethnic conflicts and wars between 1991 and 2001.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which country exited the European Union in a process popularly termed 'Brexit' following a national referendum?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union in June 2016 and formally exited on 31 January 2020.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which international forum established in 1994 conducts annual multilateral consultations on political and security matters across the Asia-Pacific region under ASEAN?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) was founded in 1994 to foster constructive dialogue on peace, security, and confidence-building in the Asia-Pacific.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which military dictator ousted Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in Pakistan in a July 1977 coup and established martial law?
questions.explanation: General Zia-ul-Haq deposed Bhutto in Operation Fair Play in July 1977 and ruled Pakistan until his death in a plane crash in 1988.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What is the capital city of Bangladesh where the historic first SAARC summit was held in December 1985?
questions.explanation: The inaugural summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) took place in Dhaka on 7-8 December 1985.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Where is the global headquarters of the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) located?
questions.explanation: UNICEF was established by the UN General Assembly in 1946 and is headquartered in New York City.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which autonomous Vienna-based international organisation is entrusted with inspecting civil nuclear power reactors to ensure safety and prevent military diversion?
questions.explanation: The IAEA was established in 1957 in Vienna, Austria, reporting to both the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

questions.question: Which multilateral arms treaty signed in 1968 prohibits non-nuclear weapon states from acquiring nuclear weapons?
questions.explanation: The NPT recognizes only the five P5 states as nuclear weapon states and forbids all other signatories from acquiring nuclear weapons.

questions.question: Which concept of security expands its focus beyond national defense to encompass threats from infectious disease epidemics, famine, and global poverty?
questions.explanation: Non-traditional security moves beyond inter-state military warfare to address threats to human survival and dignity, such as poverty, disease, and environmental disasters.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The 1987 Montreal Protocol was designed to phase out industrial chemicals that destroy which part of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol bans the production and consumption of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons that deplete the stratospheric ozone layer.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in Japan in December 1997, aimed to reduce emissions of which category of pollutants?
options: B) Plastic debris discarded in international oceans
C) Greenhouse gases that cause global warming
D) Toxic industrial heavy metal mercury effluents
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol set binding emission reduction targets for six major greenhouse gases that cause human-induced climate change.

questions.question: Which global intergovernmental organisation succeeded the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) on 1 January 1995 to regulate international trade?
questions.explanation: The WTO was established following the Marrakesh Agreement in 1995, overseeing global trade rules and resolving trade disputes among members.

questions.question: What is the phenomenon called when distinctive American or Western cultural products (jeans, Hollywood, fast food) spread globally and influence traditional lifestyles?
questions.explanation: Cultural homogenisation refers to the global spread of uniform Western consumer culture at the expense of traditional indigenous customs.

questions.question: Which Indian Prime Minister announced the implementation of the Mandal Commission's recommendations in Parliament on 7 August 1990?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Vishwanath Pratap Singh announced in the Lok Sabha on 7 August 1990 that the government would implement the Mandal Commission recommendation of 27% quota for OBCs.

questions.question: Why did political scientist Rajni Kothari characterize the first two decades of Indian democracy as the 'Congress System'?
options: A) Because all opposition political parties were legally banned by the Supreme Court of India
B) Because elections were conducted under a one-party presidential decree system
C) Because Congress functioned as a broad umbrella coalition accommodating diverse social factions and managing internal opposition within itself
D) Because the Prime Minister held the statutory authority to appoint all members of Parliament
questions.explanation: Rajni Kothari argued that the Congress system was unique: it was a dominant party containing internal factions representing different social and regional interests, providing both governance and opposition.

questions.question: How did the Government of India resolve the territorial status of the princely state of Hyderabad in September 1948?
options: A) Through an international boundary referendum conducted by the United Nations Security Council
B) By granting Hyderabad complete independence as a sovereign landlocked sultanate
C) By dividing Hyderabad equally between Pakistan and the Dominion of India
D) Through Indian Army police action (Operation Polo) that suppressed the Razakar militia and led to the Nizam's surrender
questions.explanation: The Indian armed forces entered Hyderabad on 13 September 1948 in Operation Polo, forcing the surrender of the Nizam's army and Razakars within four days.

questions.question: What major shift in agricultural strategy occurred in India in the mid-1960s under Food Minister C. Subramaniam and scientist M.S. Swaminathan?
options: A) Shifting from institutional land reforms to a technological package approach utilizing High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation
B) Abolishing all private land ownership and creating state-run collective communes
C) Banning the use of all chemical fertilizers in favor of traditional organic compost
D) Importing all wheat and rice grains exclusively from neighboring South Asian countries
questions.explanation: The government adopted a technological package strategy in 1965-66, supplying HYV seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and credit to farmers in irrigated areas to achieve food self-sufficiency.

questions.question: Why did India refuse to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) in 1968 and the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT) in 1996?
options: A) India was legally prohibited from signing any international treaties under the United Nations Charter
B) India considered them inherently discriminatory because they divided the world into nuclear 'haves' (P5) and 'have-nots' without mandating universal disarmament
C) India lacked the financial resources to pay the annual membership fee of the treaties
D) India wished to sell nuclear weapons technology to non-aligned countries across Africa
questions.explanation: India objected to the NPT and CTBT on principled grounds, pointing out that they legitimized the nuclear monopolies of the five permanent UNSC members while denying non-nuclear states the right to develop defense capabilities.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: What was the political significance of the phrase 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' that gained prominence after the 1967 state assembly elections?
options: A) It was a religious chant used by socialist parties during election rallies
B) It was a military slogan used during border patrols in the western desert sector
C) It described the rampant phenomenon of floor-crossing and political defections by legislators that destabilized state governments
D) It was an agricultural festival celebrated by tenant farmers across northern India
questions.explanation: Coined after Haryana MLA Gaya Lal switched parties three times in a single fortnight in 1967, 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' became the enduring idiom for unprincipled political defections.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the sweeping changes introduced into the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976?
options: A) Abolishing the Supreme Court of India and replacing it with a Cabinet tribunal
B) Banning all regional language publications across the territory of India
C) Declaring India a constituent province of the United Nations Trusteeship Council
D) Adding 'Secular' and 'Socialist' to the Preamble, inserting Fundamental Duties, extending parliamentary tenure to 6 years, and curtailing judicial review
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 altered the Preamble, introduced Part IVA (Fundamental Duties), extended the life of legislatures to six years, and curbed the power of judicial review.

questions.question: The military operation code-named 'Operation Blue Star' carried out in June 1984 was launched to achieve which objective?
options: A) To flush out armed Sikh militants led by Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale who had fortified the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar
B) To capture Pakistani military garrisons across the Line of Control in Jammu
C) To evict unauthorized encroachers from the municipal gardens of Chandigarh
D) To liberate the Portuguese colonial enclaves along the western coast of India
questions.explanation: Operation Blue Star was conducted from 1 to 8 June 1984 by the Indian Army to clear heavily armed militants from the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) complex in Amritsar.

questions.question: What was the major socio-political consequence of the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations across northern India?
options: A) The complete dissolution of all state legislative assemblies by the President of India
B) Massive student agitations and self-immolations in urban areas, followed by the intense political mobilization and electoral consolidation of OBCs
C) The total abolition of all reservation benefits previously granted to Scheduled Castes
D) The nationwide boycott of general elections by all national political parties
questions.explanation: The announcement triggered widespread anti-reservation student protests across north Indian cities, while simultaneously consolidating backward-caste political solidarity and giving rise to powerful regional parties.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which of the following was a primary political reason for the internal collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991?
options: A) A direct military invasion launched by NATO ground troops across the Polish border
B) The immediate bankruptcy of all Western multinational banks operating in Moscow
C) Rampant bureaucratic corruption, lack of democratic accountability, economic stagnation due to the arms race, and the surge of republican nationalisms
D) The complete cessation of all agricultural production across the Ukrainian plains
questions.explanation: The USSR suffered from economic exhaustion caused by military spending, a rigid unaccountable bureaucracy, public disillusionment, and powerful nationalist aspirations unleashed by Gorbachev's reforms.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What are the three pillars of the ASEAN Community established by Southeast Asian leaders under the Bali Concord II in 2003?
options: A) ASEAN Defense Council, ASEAN Tariff Union, and ASEAN Maritime Command
B) ASEAN Monetary Authority, ASEAN Space Agency, and ASEAN Labour League
C) ASEAN Diplomatic Forum, ASEAN Free Trade Union, and ASEAN Justice Council
D) ASEAN Security Community, ASEAN Economic Community, and ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community
questions.explanation: In 2003, ASEAN leaders established the ASEAN Community based on three distinct pillars: Security, Economic, and Socio-Cultural cooperation.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: How did the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War transform the geopolitical map of South Asia?
options: A) It bifurcated Pakistan, created the independent sovereign republic of Bangladesh, and established India as the undisputed pre-eminent power in South Asia
B) It resulted in the permanent annexation of East Pakistan as a constituent state of India
C) It caused the dissolution of the United Nations Security Council in New York
D) It forced Sri Lanka and Nepal to merge their defense commands with Pakistan
questions.explanation: The 1971 war dismembered Pakistan, birthed sovereign Bangladesh under Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, and decisively demonstrated India's conventional military superiority in the region.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the primary argument against the veto power exercised by the five permanent members (P5) of the UN Security Council?
options: A) It allows non-permanent member states to overrule decisions taken by the General Assembly
B) It is undemocratic, paralyzes the Security Council when permanent members' interests conflict, and prevents effective action in global humanitarian crises
C) It requires the UN to spend all of its annual operational budget on European projects
D) It forces all member states to maintain standing nuclear ballistic arsenals
questions.explanation: Critics argue that the P5 veto is an undemocratic anachronism of 1945 that frequently paralyzes the UN during severe international conflicts when P5 national interests are involved.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'Refugees' and 'Migrants' under international humanitarian law?
options: A) Refugees leave voluntarily to pursue university degrees, while migrants are forcibly expelled by the military
B) Refugees are protected exclusively by the World Bank, while migrants are registered with NATO
C) Refugees flee across borders to escape persecution, war, or violence and cannot return safely, whereas migrants generally move voluntarily for economic or personal reasons
D) Refugees must pay international transit taxes, whereas migrants travel without national passports
questions.explanation: Refugees are forced to cross borders to escape life-threatening persecution or conflict and are protected by the 1951 Refugee Convention; economic migrants move voluntarily.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What is the central finding of the 1972 Club of Rome report 'The Limits to Growth' regarding global industrial expansion?
options: A) That modern technology can infinitely produce fossil fuels without any environmental cost
B) That industrial manufacturing will completely eliminate all atmospheric pollution by the year 2000
C) That developing nations should abandon agriculture and import food exclusively from Western Europe
D) That exponential economic and population growth will inevitably collide with the finite resource carrying capacity of planet Earth, leading to ecological collapse
questions.explanation: Using computer modeling, 'The Limits to Growth' demonstrated that unchecked industrialization and resource consumption would overshoot Earth's environmental limits within a century.

questions.question: What was the significance of the massive civil society demonstrations during the WTO Ministerial Conference in Seattle in November 1999?
options: A) It dramatized global grassroots opposition to neo-liberal trade deregulation, bringing labor, environmental, and consumer groups together in protest
B) It resulted in the immediate military abolition of all sovereign national borders in North America
C) It led to the complete dissolution of the United Nations General Assembly in New York
D) It forced the World Trade Organization to convert all international trade into physical gold barter
questions.explanation: The 'Battle of Seattle' in 1999 brought global anti-globalisation movements into worldwide prominence, shutting down WTO talks and questioning corporate-led free trade.

questions.question: In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati judgment of April 1973, by what narrow judicial majority was the Basic Structure doctrine affirmed by the 13-judge Supreme Court bench?
questions.explanation: The 13-judge Constitution Bench ruled by a wafer-thin 7:6 majority that while Parliament can amend any provision of the Constitution, it cannot alter its Basic Structure.

questions.question: Under the 1985 Rajiv Gandhi - Longowal Accord (Punjab Accord), which specific contentious issues were agreed upon to resolve the Punjab crisis?
options: A) The immediate creation of an independent sovereign state of Khalistan outside India
B) The complete merger of Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh into a unified province
C) The transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab, reference of the Ravi-Beas river waters dispute to a tribunal, and rehabilitation of affected individuals
D) The permanent military occupation of the Golden Temple complex by central armed police forces
questions.explanation: The accord provided for Chandigarh's transfer to Punjab, an autonomous tribunal (Eradi Tribunal) to adjudicate Ravi-Beas river waters, and compensation to innocent victims.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In December 1991, the leaders of which eight additional former Soviet republics met in Kazakhstan to sign a protocol expanding the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)?
questions.explanation: On 21 December 1991, eleven former Soviet republics signed the Alma-Ata Protocol in Kazakhstan, formally confirming the dissolution of the USSR and broadening the CIS.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which historic treaty signed in 1957 by France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg created the European Economic Community (Common Market)?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Rome was signed in March 1957, establishing the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom).

questions.question: Which bilateral arms limitation treaty signed in 1972 between US President Richard Nixon and Soviet General Secretary Leonid Brezhnev placed strict ceilings on anti-ballistic missile defensive interceptor systems?
questions.explanation: The 1972 ABM Treaty limited the US and USSR to two anti-ballistic missile deployment complexes each to preserve nuclear deterrence through Mutual Assured Destruction (MAD).
